paragraphs: Automated red-teaming trains an attacker model to find prompts that provoke harmful responses, supplying examples for safety training. A recurring problem is that the attacker discovers a few effective prompt types and keeps returning to them. Even training objectives intended to encourage diversity can stop rewarding meaningful exploration once these successful patterns emerge.

Active Attacks changes the training environment by periodically safety fine-tuning the target model on collected attacks. As the target learns to resist those prompts, the attacker must explore harder cases. This creates an evolving curriculum through changes to the target itself. The method is designed as an addition that integrates with existing reinforcement-learning objectives.

In the reported comparison, cross-attack success increased from 0.07% to 31.28% against GFlowNets, the previous leading approach, while computation increased by 6%. The finding supports adapting the target during attack generation as a way to encourage exploration. Its significance is the combination of a much stronger reported attack signal and a relatively small additional training cost.
icml-2026-active-attacks-red-teaming-llm.tldr: Active Attacks periodically strengthens the target model during red-teaming, pushing attackers toward harder prompts with a small reported increase in computation.

paragraphs: Systems built from multiple language-model agents need decisions about both how agents connect and how they behave. Automated design methods can improve task performance, but robustness often receives less attention. AutoRAS makes resistance to external attacks and internal failures part of the system-design process, alongside the ability to complete tasks successfully.

The framework represents a system as a sequence of symbolic primitives. These primitives jointly describe structural connections and behavioral actions, giving the learning process a common representation for both. AutoRAS optimizes the sequence using safety signals obtained from actual executions together with flow-based objectives applied to entire sequences. Robustness therefore informs the process that generates the workflow.

The experiments report the strongest performance among the evaluated approaches in both ordinary and adversarial settings, with the smallest deterioration under attack. Additional analyses report transferability, stable optimization, stability across primitive sets, and favorable cost trade-offs. These findings support treating robust agent design as a learnable problem over explicit system components, rather than leaving robustness for a later adjustment.
icml-2026-autoras-learning-robust-agenti.tldr: AutoRAS learns agent workflows from symbolic components while incorporating execution-based safety feedback into system design.

paragraphs: Generating a CAD program from a written description becomes difficult when dimensions are missing or geometric constraints contradict one another. A model that immediately writes code may silently invent measurements. ProCAD addresses this problem before code generation by checking whether the requested object has a sufficiently consistent specification.

The system separates clarification from implementation. A clarifying agent audits the description and asks focused questions only when they are needed to resolve specification problems. A coding agent then converts the resulting specification into an executable CadQuery program. The coding agent is fine-tuned on a curated text-to-CadQuery dataset, while the clarifying agent learns from supervised examples of clarification interactions.

The experiments report greater robustness to ambiguous prompts with low interaction overhead. ProCAD outperforms evaluated frontier closed-source models, including Claude Sonnet 4.5, with a 79.9% reduction in mean Chamfer distance and an invalidity ratio falling from 4.8% to 0.9%. Together, these results indicate that resolving ambiguity early can improve both geometric agreement and program validity.
icml-2026-clarify-before-you-draw-proact.tldr: ProCAD asks targeted clarification questions before generating CAD code, improving geometric accuracy and validity on ambiguous requests.

paragraphs: This paper studies how to select a valuable collection of items under a total cost budget while protecting sensitive individual data. The objective is submodular, meaning that additional items exhibit diminishing returns. The authors consider both monotone objectives, where adding items does not reduce value, and non-monotone objectives, where it can.

For monotone objectives, the paper gives a differentially private algorithm with the optimal approximation ratio of 1−1/e. Its guarantees also improve additive error and query complexity over earlier work. A second algorithm offers greater efficiency with a weaker approximation ratio of one half. These alternatives expose a concrete trade-off between computational efficiency and the strength of the utility guarantee.

For non-monotone objectives, the authors present what they describe as the first differentially private algorithm with provable guarantees. It achieves a one-quarter approximation in expectation, with additive error comparable to the best known for monotone objectives. The expectation qualification and additive error are part of the guarantee: the result does not promise a fixed fraction of the optimum on every run without adjustment.
icml-2026-differentially-private-submodu.tldr: The paper improves private budget-constrained submodular optimization and provides a qualified first guarantee for non-monotone objectives.

paragraphs: Tabular foundation models can make predictions by taking training examples as context, without updating their parameters for each new dataset. This makes their use different from fitting a separate model through repeated parameter updates. However, transformer attention has quadratic complexity in dataset size, creating substantial time and memory costs as the context grows.

TACO addresses that bottleneck by learning to compress the training dataset into a latent representation. The compression is trained end to end, making it part of the overall modeling approach. The central idea is to reduce the amount of contextual information the tabular model must process while retaining the information needed for useful predictions.

On TabArena, the method reports inference up to 94 times faster and memory consumption up to 97% lower than the compared state-of-the-art tabular Transformer, without significant performance degradation. The abstract also reports better scaling with dataset size and stronger performance than other baselines. These are reported maximum efficiency gains, supporting learned dataset compression as a practical route to larger tabular workloads.
icml-2026-end-to-end-compression-for-tab.tldr: TACO compresses tabular training data into latent representations, reporting much faster inference and lower memory use while largely retaining predictive performance.

paragraphs: Finding a particular paragraph, table, or image across connected documents can require several retrieval steps. A single similarity measure may miss what matters at different stages of that search, while a fixed plan gives the retriever little room to recover when it takes an unhelpful path. This paper treats retrieval as a sequence of decisions that can change with context.

Its history-aware backtracking mechanism retains information from unsuccessful traversals. Returning to an earlier point therefore does not erase what the agent learned about the failed route. The context of previous failures informs subsequent decisions, making a dead end part of the evidence available for continuing the search.

The framework also makes computation a decision variable. A cost-aware orchestrator manages the trade-off between retrieval accuracy and inference expense, escalating to more intensive language-model reasoning when prior failure justifies it. The contribution described in the abstract is this combination of adaptive recovery and selective reasoning effort: the search can revise both where it goes and how much computation it spends.
icml-2026-failure-is-feedback-history-aw.tldr: Failure is Feedback uses unsuccessful retrieval paths to guide backtracking and decide when more expensive reasoning is warranted.

paragraphs: Personalized federated learning aims to give different devices models suited to their own data distributions. Many existing approaches require each device to hold labeled examples for training or fine-tuning. FLowDUP addresses clients that have only unlabeled data, generating their personalized model through a forward pass instead of requiring local labeled adaptation.

The generated parameters lie in a low-dimensional subspace. Restricting personalization to this smaller space enables efficient communication and computation while still allowing models to differ across clients. The training objective is designed so that clients with labels and clients without labels can both contribute, extending participation beyond devices that can supply supervised examples.

The objective is motivated by a new transductive multi-task PAC-Bayesian generalization bound that provides performance guarantees for unlabeled clients. Experiments report strong performance across datasets with different forms of client heterogeneity, and ablations examine the contributions of individual components. The paper therefore combines a theoretical basis for unlabeled personalization with empirical evidence that the approach works across varied client populations.
icml-2026-federated-learning-with-unlabe.tldr: FLowDUP generates personalized federated models from unlabeled data in one forward pass using a low-dimensional parameter space.

paragraphs: Large pretrained models often come with a fixed computational cost even when deployment settings have very different budgets. Building a separate model from scratch for each setting is expensive. FlexRank addresses this mismatch by extracting a family of nested components from an existing model, allowing deployment to use only the components that fit the available budget.

The method combines low-rank weight decomposition with consolidation based on component importance. The resulting submodels are nested and ordered to provide increasing capabilities. A smaller configuration uses a more limited selection, while a larger configuration activates additional components. This gives the pretrained model a structure that supports multiple operating costs.

The paper presents this as a way to train once and deploy across budgets, with a gradual trade-off between performance and cost. Its contribution is the construction of adaptable submodels from pretrained weights, avoiding training from scratch for every budget. The approach is motivated by the deployment burden of large language models and vision transformers.
icml-2026-flexrank-nested-low-rank-knowl.tldr: FlexRank decomposes pretrained models into nested components that can be selectively activated to fit different computational budgets.

paragraphs: Synthetic tables need to preserve relationships among columns as well as patterns within individual columns. Standard diffusion models leave much of that relational learning implicit. Geometry-Aware Tabular Diffusion makes it explicit by computing pairwise angles and lengths from differences between column values, then using these quantities as both model inputs and auxiliary prediction targets.

The MLP version reports state-of-the-art benchmark performance with 3.5 times fewer parameters on average. Across ten datasets, it wins eight Shape comparisons, seven Trend comparisons, and nine downstream-utility comparisons, with Shape and Trend errors reduced by 27% and 20%. These findings connect the relational training signal to both data-quality measures and usefulness for downstream prediction.

The same default loss weights also improve GNN and Transformer denoisers, with gains in 27 of 30 Shape comparisons and 25 of 30 Trend comparisons. A matched ablation attributes the gains to supervision rather than extra inputs or model capacity. That result supports explicit relational targets as a training principle that transfers across denoiser architectures.
icml-2026-geometry-aware-tabular-diffusi.tldr: GATD explicitly teaches tabular diffusion models relationships between columns, improving reported synthesis quality and downstream utility across architectures.

paragraphs: TTT-Discover studies how a language model can search for an exceptional solution to a particular scientific or technical problem. Instead of keeping the model frozen during search, it continues reinforcement learning at test time using experience from that problem. The target is one outstanding result for the current task, rather than strong average performance across future tasks.

That goal shapes both the learning objective and the search procedure, which prioritize the most promising solutions. The work focuses on problems with continuous rewards. Evaluations cover mathematics, GPU kernel engineering, algorithm design, and single-cell analysis, and the authors report results for every problem they attempted.

The method achieves new best results on almost all attempted problems, including kernel results up to twice as fast as prior work. Experts or competition organizers review the solutions. All results use the open gpt-oss-120b model, with public reproduction code and reported training costs of a few hundred dollars per problem. The findings support task-specific learning as a productive addition to test-time search.
icml-2026-learning-to-discover-at-test-t.tldr: TTT-Discover continues reinforcement learning on a specific test problem to search for exceptional solutions, reporting new best results on almost all attempted tasks.

paragraphs: Memory agents decide how to process, store, and retrieve information instead of following a fixed memory pipeline. Training these decisions is difficult when the agent performs many operations before receiving feedback. A final success or failure signal provides little immediate guidance about which earlier memory decisions contributed to the outcome.

Mem-T combines an autonomous agent with a lightweight hierarchical memory database for updating memories and retrieving them through multiple turns over streaming inputs. Its training framework, MoT-GRPO, uses a tree of memory operations to propagate final feedback back to individual steps. Hindsight credit assignment supplies denser supervision, supporting joint optimization of memory construction and retrieval.

Experiments report improvements of up to 14.94% over frameworks such as A-Mem and Mem0. Mem-T also occupies a favorable accuracy-efficiency trade-off and uses approximately 24.45% fewer inference tokens per query than GAM without sacrificing performance. These findings suggest that better feedback for intermediate memory decisions can improve both answer quality and the cost of using memory.
icml-2026-mem-t-densifying-rewards-for-l.tldr: Mem-T turns delayed memory-task feedback into step-level training signals, improving reported performance while reducing retrieval-related inference costs.

paragraphs: Unsupervised environment design chooses training situations for a reinforcement-learning agent as its abilities develop. Its effectiveness depends on recognizing which environments offer useful learning opportunities. Existing approaches often estimate this through indirect signals that can be biased, noisy, or expensive to calculate. PACE evaluates environments through the parameter changes they induce during learning.

For a candidate level, PACE performs a provisional policy update and measures the squared Euclidean size of the resulting parameter change. That score determines entry into a buffer that accounts for staleness, and rank-based prioritization controls replay. The resulting curriculum changes with the agent because an environment's score depends on its effect on the current policy.

The authors describe this optimization-based score as a low-variance measure of realized learning progress that requires no additional environment rollouts. Experiments on MiniGrid and Craftax show consistent improvements over established environment-design baselines in zero-shot generalization across multiple out-of-distribution evaluation protocols. The results support using the agent's actual update behavior to guide adaptive training-level selection.
icml-2026-pace-parameter-change-for-unsu.tldr: PACE selects reinforcement-learning environments using the parameter changes caused by provisional updates, improving reported zero-shot generalization.

paragraphs: Reasoning models face a resource-allocation problem: additional thinking can help, but its value varies across queries and reasoning paths. Re-FORC predicts expected future reward as a function of how many additional thinking tokens a model uses. This provides a forecast of the benefit of continuing, rather than relying only on a fixed token allowance.

The method trains a lightweight adapter on reasoning models. Prediction improves with longer reasoning and larger models in the reported experiments. Its forecasts support stopping unpromising chains, selecting a model and thinking length together, and allocating extra computation adaptively. Cost-per-token thresholds provide length control, while the method also estimates computation time upfront.

Early stopping reduces compute by up to 26% versus fixed-budget cutoffs while maintaining accuracy. Joint selection reaches peak accuracy 1.7 percentage points above the largest model alone and matches its accuracy with up to 12% less compute. Adaptive scaling improves accuracy by 9.9 percentage points on average at maximum compute over confidence-based baselines, supporting reward forecasts as a useful allocation signal.
icml-2026-re-forc-adaptive-reward-predic.tldr: Re-FORC predicts the value of additional thinking tokens to adapt reasoning length, model choice, and computation allocation.

paragraphs: This paper distinguishes following instructions in a final answer from controlling the text of a reasoning trace. The second ability matters for monitoring: a model that can selectively suppress signs of misbehavior in its chain of thought could make oversight harder. The authors introduce CoT-Control to measure that ability directly.

The evaluated reasoning models follow constraints less reliably in their reasoning than in their outputs. For a request to solve a genetics problem without using the word “chromosome,” Claude Sonnet 4.5 complies only 5% of the time. Controllability is higher in larger models and decreases with more reinforcement-learning training, more test-time computation, and harder problems.

Failures persist when models receive incentives to evade monitors, and adversarial prompt optimization does not meaningfully improve control. Being told about monitoring produces a slight increase. The authors interpret the overall findings with cautious optimism, while emphasizing that the mechanism remains poorly understood. Low observed controllability supports continued interest in reasoning-trace monitoring, alongside tracking whether future models gain greater control.
icml-2026-reasoning-models-struggle-to-c.tldr: CoT-Control finds that tested reasoning models struggle to obey constraints on their reasoning traces, offering qualified encouragement for trace-based monitoring.

paragraphs: Pre-propagation graph neural networks spread node information through the graph before training, then learn dense transformations for individual nodes. This separation supports mini-batches without dependencies between nodes and avoids repeatedly performing sparse matrix operations. It also suits accelerators designed for dense computation, making the architecture attractive when training efficiency matters.

The difficulty is predictive performance: existing pre-propagation models lag behind message-passing networks on common benchmarks, particularly heterophilic graphs, where linked nodes can differ in relevant characteristics. The paper introduces more robust diffusion operators for preprocessing and a scheme that re-propagates hidden representations a small number of times during training.

These changes improve both validation and test accuracy in the reported evaluations. The resulting models match the accuracy of message-passing graph networks while retaining training efficiency. The contribution shows that the accuracy gap can be addressed by improving how graph information is initially spread and selectively revisiting propagation during learning, preserving the main computational appeal of the pre-propagation design.
icml-2026-revisiting-pre-propagation-gnn.tldr: Improved graph diffusion and occasional hidden-state propagation let pre-propagation GNNs match reported message-passing accuracy while retaining efficient training.

paragraphs: An image model can be designed so that rotating or flipping its input produces a corresponding transformation in its internal features. This property, equivariance, preserves a structured relationship between input orientation and representation. The paper studies how to build that behavior into a vision transformer for a discrete set of rotations and reflections.

Earlier work on these symmetries has concentrated largely on convolutional neural networks. REViT examines the obstacles to achieving equivariance in transformers and proposes a simpler implementation using convolutional attention. Its feature maps preserve rotational, flip, and positional symmetries, giving the architecture explicit structure for handling changes in input orientation.

Image-classification experiments show that the approach outperforms the compared methods for constructing discrete roto-reflection equivariant networks. The reported finding concerns classification, while the motivation also discusses the relevance of such models to object detection. The central contribution is an architectural route for bringing these symmetry-preserving properties into vision transformers, together with evidence that the resulting design can improve classification performance.
icml-2026-revit-roto-reflection-equivari.tldr: REViT uses convolutional attention to build a vision transformer that preserves discrete rotation and reflection symmetries.

paragraphs: Capability evaluations can be misleading if a model deliberately performs below its abilities, a behavior called sandbagging. Cross-Context Consistency, or C³, investigates whether this behavior can be detected from responses alone. It compares behavior across paraphrases of the same question, using inconsistencies as evidence relevant to deliberate underperformance.

The framework is motivated by an asymmetry between genuine confusion and strategically pretending to be incapable. The latter requires choices about how to fail, which can differ across contexts. C³ allows different consistency measures and aggregation rules. The paper demonstrates a simple version that averages cosine distances between response embeddings, requiring neither training data nor model-specific adaptation.

Evaluations include prompted and fine-tuned sandbagging, with both explicitly instructed and more naturalistic setups. C³ retains a classification signal in settings where other black-box methods fail. These findings support consistency checking as a useful detection mechanism in the evaluated scenarios. The reported result is a discriminative signal from patterns across responses, rather than a claim that any single inconsistency establishes deliberate deception.
icml-2026-same-question-different-lies-c.tldr: C³ detects signals of deliberate underperformance by comparing how consistently a model responds to paraphrased questions.

paragraphs: Visual self-supervised learning often trains representations by aligning continuous features from different views of an image. This paper instead treats learning as communication between teacher and student networks through a binary channel with fixed capacity. The student learns to predict the teacher's multi-label binary messages, making the information exchanged explicitly discrete.

An element-wise binary cross-entropy objective encourages agreement on the message, while coding-rate regularization encourages effective use of the limited channel. Periodically reinitializing the projection head strengthens the effect by encouraging embeddings that remain useful across different discrete encodings. Together, these choices aim to give the learned representation more structure than continuous agreement alone provides.

Experiments report consistent gains over continuous-agreement baselines in image classification, retrieval, and dense visual prediction, as well as adaptation under domain shift. Analysis of the binary messages finds compact, informative codes that capture semantic factors reusable across classes. The findings therefore concern both stronger backbone representations and the structure of the discrete messages used to train them.
icml-2026-self-supervised-learning-as-di.tldr: Training a student to predict a teacher's capacity-limited binary messages produces structured visual representations with reported gains across several tasks.

paragraphs: Asynchronous stochastic gradient descent allows distributed workers to contribute updates with delays. This paper analyzes how well the resulting model generalizes using on-average model stability, which concerns average sensitivity to changes in training data. The aim is to obtain informative guarantees under fewer restrictive assumptions about the data, parameters, and update process.

For convex, smooth objectives, the analysis removes requirements for Lipschitz continuity, bounded noise, and bounded parameter or data domains. It allows randomly partitioned data and arbitrary delays, while explicitly accounting for worker participation. In balanced regimes, the bounds recover the minimax-optimal rate O(1/√(mn)), where mn is the sample size; low-noise conditions imply faster rates.

The paper also extends the analysis to objectives with Hölder-continuous gradients and to heterogeneous data through random ASGD. Both extensions yield non-vacuous excess-risk guarantees, and experiments support the theoretical findings. The contribution is a more flexible account of generalization in asynchronous learning, with rate improvements tied to the stated balance and noise conditions.
icml-2026-sharper-generalization-guarant.tldr: The paper derives sharper asynchronous-SGD generalization bounds under weaker assumptions, with optimal rates in balanced regimes and faster rates under low noise.

paragraphs: Editing several separate parts of an image at once requires each instruction to affect its intended region without interfering with the others. Existing flow-based editors struggle with this setting. The paper attributes the problem to globally conditioned velocity fields and joint attention, which mix information from concurrent edits during image transformation.

Instance-Disentangled Attention addresses that mixing by partitioning joint attention operations. It binds each instance-specific text instruction to its corresponding spatial region while the model estimates the velocity field that drives editing. The design targets the internal interaction between instructions and image regions, supporting independent local edits within a single editing pass.

The authors evaluate the method on natural images and introduce a benchmark of text-heavy infographics with region-level instructions. Results show improved separation and locality of edits while preserving coherence across the full output. These findings suggest that controlling attention at the instance level can help flow-based editors handle multiple simultaneous requests without losing the overall consistency of the generated image.
icml-2026-shifting-the-breaking-point-of.tldr: Instance-Disentangled Attention links separate editing instructions to their image regions, improving simultaneous local edits in flow-matching models.

paragraphs: Text diffusion models generate text through iterative denoising, creating a different safety-control problem from autoregressive generation. The paper argues that existing approaches geared toward autoregressive models do not adequately address this process. Its Safety-Aware Denoiser integrates safety guidance directly into the denoising steps used to produce the final text.

SAD operates at inference time and incorporates safety constraints into the denoiser without retraining the underlying diffusion model. The proposed modification steers the final sample toward regions of text space that are provably safe under the framework's constraints. This makes the safety guidance part of generation itself while keeping adaptation lightweight and avoiding expensive model retraining.

The evaluation examines unsafe content through a hazard taxonomy, along with memorization and jailbreak behavior. Experiments report substantial reductions in unsafe generations while preserving quality and fluency, outperforming the compared methods. The theoretical safe-region claim and the empirical reductions serve distinct roles: one characterizes the framework's constrained target, while the other demonstrates its observed behavior on the evaluated safety tasks.
icml-2026-the-safety-aware-denoiser-for-.tldr: SAD adds safety constraints to text diffusion denoising at inference time, reducing reported unsafe generations without retraining the model.

paragraphs: Do-calculus provides rules for transforming queries about interventions into equivalent probability expressions. The difficulty lies in deciding which rules to apply and in what order. This paper makes that reasoning structure explicit through derivation graphs, which describe how rule applications connect and combine across equivalent observational and interventional expressions.

The graphs characterize the full space of probabilities that are equivalent under do-calculus. Their structure leads to a simple procedure using at most four applications of its rules. This result gives a compact way to organize transformations within the characterized space, replacing an otherwise difficult problem of choosing and arranging successive rule applications.

The authors also apply identification algorithms to equivalent forms of a causal query. These different starting expressions can produce multiple valid estimands for the same causal quantity, meaning different probability-based formulas for the same target. The paper shows how this can ultimately yield more efficient estimators. Thus, the structure of symbolic causal reasoning has consequences for how effectively the target quantity is estimated.
icml-2026-unveiling-the-structure-of-do-.tldr: Derivation graphs organize equivalent do-calculus expressions, enabling a short rule-application procedure and alternative estimands that yield more efficient estimators.

paragraphs: Long-context language-model inference is constrained by the memory demands of the key-value cache. Sparse self-speculative decoding speeds generation by drafting tokens using only part of that cache, then verifying them in parallel against the full cache. Verification preserves the lossless behavior of this approach, but selecting a useful cache subset introduces its own overhead.

Vegas reuses information already computed during verification to identify important cache entries. Subsequent drafting attends only to those entries. This connects the verification and drafting stages more closely: the full-cache check also supplies guidance for the next sparse draft, reducing the need for a separate cache-selection procedure.

The method improves draft-token acceptance while keeping selection overhead low. Reported decoding-throughput gains range from 1.25 to 2.81 times over default vLLM and from 1.15 to 1.29 times over leading sparse self-speculative methods. The findings show that verification can serve two purposes at once, checking candidate tokens and informing a more efficient next round of drafting.
icml-2026-vegas-self-speculative-decodin.tldr: Vegas reuses verification attention to choose cache entries for speculative drafting, improving token acceptance and decoding throughput.

paragraphs: Web agents trained on recorded browser interactions can struggle on unfamiliar websites and tasks. Training is also expensive when trajectories contain redundant steps and lengthy accessibility-tree descriptions. Weasel addresses both issues by choosing a fixed-budget subset of training steps that balances the importance of individual examples with diversity across examples.

Its selection objective considers differences in states, websites, and interaction patterns, and a greedy algorithm solves the selection problem efficiently. The method also prunes accessibility trees around the ground-truth action target. For reasoning-native models, it replaces expert traces with model-generated rationales that better match the model's style, addressing a separate mismatch in the training material.

Experiments use AgentTrek and NNetNav data, evaluate on WebArena, WorkArena, and MiniWob, and cover three language models. Weasel improves out-of-domain performance while producing approximately 9.7–12.5 times faster training than standard fine-tuning. The findings support selecting informative, varied examples and shortening their state descriptions as complementary ways to improve generalization and reduce offline training cost.
icml-2026-weasel-out-of-domain-generaliz.tldr: Weasel selects important, diverse browser-training steps and prunes their context, improving reported generalization with roughly 9.7–12.5 times faster training.

paragraphs: Single-step retrosynthesis asks for a possible preceding reaction that could produce a target molecule. Existing benchmarks commonly compare predictions with one published answer using Top-K accuracy. The paper argues that this misses the open-ended nature of synthesis planning, where a chemically plausible proposal may differ from the recorded procedure.

The proposed benchmark evaluates general-purpose and chemistry-specialized language models with ChemCensor, a metric focused on chemical plausibility. This changes what counts as a useful prediction by emphasizing whether a proposed reaction is plausible rather than whether it exactly reproduces a single reference. The aim is to better reflect how people assess possible synthesis plans.

The authors also introduce CREED, a training dataset containing millions of reaction records validated with ChemCensor. A model trained on this resource improves over the language-model baselines under the proposed benchmark. The work therefore links a revised evaluation criterion to a corresponding training resource, with the reported improvement specifically measured through this plausibility-oriented framework.
icml-2026-when-single-answer-is-not-enou.tldr: ChemCensor evaluates retrosynthesis by chemical plausibility, while the CREED dataset supports training a model that improves under this new benchmark.
